phases.name: Year 1
phases.subtitle: Explore
phases.description: Engineering & Physics Foundations — Build STEM literacy, explore electrical engineering careers, and develop analytical skills.

milestones.label: Explore electrical engineering career pathways
milestones.description: Introduction to engineering disciplines with emphasis on electrical engineering applications in power systems, telecommunications, signal processing, control systems, and semiconductor devices.

milestones.label: Build calculus foundations for engineering
milestones.description: Functions, limits, derivatives, and integration. Mathematical foundation for circuit analysis, electromagnetics, and signal processing.

milestones.label: Master general chemistry for engineers
milestones.description: Atomic structure, chemical bonding, and electrochemistry. Foundation for semiconductor physics and materials science in electrical engineering.

milestones.label: Join IEEE student branch
milestones.description: Join the IEEE student branch, NSBE, or SWE. Participate in electronics projects, power systems tours, and networking events with electrical engineers.

milestones.label: Study physics foundations — electromagnetism
milestones.description: Electricity, magnetism, optics, and modern physics. Foundation for electromagnetics, circuit theory, and semiconductor device physics.

phases.name: Year 2
phases.subtitle: Engage
phases.description: Core Electrical Engineering Sciences — Master circuit analysis, electronics, and signals and systems.

milestones.label: Master circuit analysis
milestones.description: DC and AC circuit analysis, Kirchhoff's laws, Thevenin/Norton equivalents, frequency response, and transient analysis. Students analyze circuits using SPICE simulation software.

milestones.label: Study electronics and semiconductor devices
milestones.description: Diode circuits, BJT and MOSFET amplifiers, biasing, and small-signal analysis. Students design and build transistor amplifier circuits in the electronics lab.

milestones.label: Tour power plants and telecommunications facilities
milestones.description: Visit regional power generation facilities, substations, and telecommunications infrastructure with IEEE chapter. Connect theory to real electrical engineering practice.

milestones.label: Master signals and systems
milestones.description: Continuous and discrete-time signals, Fourier analysis, Laplace and Z-transforms, and LTI system analysis. Foundation for communications, control, and signal processing.

milestones.label: Study digital logic and microprocessors
milestones.description: Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential logic, FPGA implementation, and microprocessor interfacing for electrical engineering applications.

phases.name: Year 3
phases.subtitle: Develop
phases.description: Advanced EE Specialization & Professional Experience — Master power systems, communications, or control systems, and complete internship.

milestones.label: Master electromagnetics
milestones.description: Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic wave propagation, transmission lines, waveguides, and antenna fundamentals. Students design and simulate electromagnetic structures.

milestones.label: Study power systems engineering
milestones.description: Power generation, transmission, distribution, load flow analysis, and renewable energy integration. Students analyze power system stability and design protection schemes.

milestones.label: Compete in IEEE design or robotics competition
milestones.description: Participate in IEEE regional design competition, robotics challenge, or student paper competition. Develop teamwork, innovation, and technical presentation skills.

milestones.label: Complete summer electrical engineering internship
milestones.description: Secure and complete an internship at a utility company, semiconductor firm, telecommunications company, or defense contractor. Apply EE skills in professional practice.

milestones.label: Study control systems engineering
milestones.description: Classical and modern control theory, feedback systems, stability analysis, PID controllers, and state-space methods. Students design control systems for industrial and renewable energy applications.

phases.name: Year 4
phases.subtitle: Launch
phases.description: Capstone Design & Career Launch — Complete senior design project, prepare for FE exam, and launch EE career.

milestones.label: Execute senior design capstone project
milestones.description: Complete a year-long electrical engineering design project. Teams design, build, test, and demonstrate a system solving a real engineering problem with industry or research sponsor support.

milestones.label: Prepare for FE exam and professional licensure
milestones.description: Prepare for the NCEES FE Electrical exam through review courses and practice exams. Begin the path toward PE licensure.

milestones.label: Serve as peer mentor and IEEE chapter leader
milestones.description: Mentor underclassmen in electrical engineering, lead IEEE chapter activities, and organize lab workshops, tech talks, and career panels.

milestones.label: Develop career placement portfolio
milestones.description: Assemble a career launch package including technical resume, design project portfolio, lab reports, FE exam status, and documented professional network.

milestones.label: Complete exit assessment and career activation
milestones.description: Complete the CoE Electrical Engineering Exit Assessment demonstrating ABET outcomes. Finalize career activation documenting job offers, graduate admissions, or FE exam results.
